place_info.title: Cooper's Old Time Pit Bar-B-Que
place_info.address: 217 Congress Ave., Austin, TX 78701, United States

reviews.snippet:
If you’re looking for the classic Texas BBQ experience, Cooper’s delivers. The atmosphere is exactly what you’d hope for—rustic, no-frills, communal tables, and a steady line of people there for one thing: meat.

I ordered the brisket, beef rib, mac and cheese, and BBQ sauce. The standout was the beef rib. It was massive, smoky, tender, and packed with flavor. The brisket was juicy with a great bark and plenty of richness from the fat cap, although a few slices were slightly saltier than I would have preferred.

The mac and cheese was creamy and comforting, but fairly standard compared to the quality of the meat. The BBQ sauce was thin, tangy, and vinegar-forward—good for cutting through the richness, though I found the meat didn’t really need much help.

One thing first-time visitors should know is that ordering by weight can get expensive quickly. It’s easy to end up with more meat than you intended, so keep an eye on what’s being sliced. The free pickles, beans, bread, and onions are a nice touch and help round out the meal.

The atmosphere is lively and authentically Texan, and the staff were helpful despite the cafeteria-style setup. While it may not be the absolute best BBQ in Texas, it’s a very solid representation of the style and well worth a visit if you’re in Austin.

reviews.snippet:
Old school classic BBQ in a saloon like atmosphere that feels very Texas--in the best way.

Food: 4.5 Service: 4.5 Atmosphere: 4.5
Cost to worth it rating: 2.5 (can get more expensive than you expect but good stuff--2 people getting 6 pork ribs, 1/2 brisket, few sides, ice tea was $100)
Opentableable: no reservations
Return worthiness: yes

Highlights:
- Solid BBQ and fun atmosphere
- Brisket: super tender and juicy with a big fat layer to insulate the flavor. My fave type of bbq of any style (to the chagrin of my pulled pork Carolina hub). 4.5 stars
- Pork ribs: longer than I thought and not as tender but great flavor. 4 stars
- Sauce: thin and a bit tangy and some spice. 3.5 stars
- Mac and cheese: the creamy velveeta-like version. If you get the Jalapeño bacon version prep for the hidden spice and big slices of bacon.  3.25 stars
- Corn on the cob: black peppery which I like but maybe not for everyone. Could've been a bit fresher. 3 stars
- Loaves of bread to make it a sandwich
- Butcher paper as your plate to eat on the shared picnic table benches
- Bar in the middle
- Pies: sadly didn't have room for any but cool they had trays of different types

Midlights:
- For a newbie hard to know how much to order of each bbq item, but staff was helpful

Lowlights:
- Wish could've tried more meats

reviews.snippet:
A long-running Texas barbecue joint known (for better or for worse) as being George W. Bush’s favorite, Cooper’s largely lived up to its reputation. The restaurant has a classic look (wood, brick, and ducts), and the menu – meats priced by the pound on a chalkboard – adds to the retro appeal. Those meats are cut to order by a pitmaster. After making your selection, you proceed down a cafeteria-style line and pick your sides. Sauce, pickles, and Wonder Bread are free.

We opted for some brisket, a jalapeno sausage link, potato salad, and creamed corn. The brisket was tender and flavorful if a bit fatty while the sausage boasted a firm bite and a winning combination of spicy and cheesy. Unexpectedly, the creamed corn ended up being a highlight. If that’s a side you usually avoid, Cooper’s version may end up converting you.

That said, the potato salad was nothing special and the sauce was very tomato-and-vinegar-forward. As to be expected given Cooper’s location and reputation, prices are also quite high (as in almost $40 a pound for brisket). That’s not outrageous for a “name” BBQ place in Austin though if I had to pay that after waiting in a long line, I might walk away disappointed.

Cooper’s is not the best Texas BBQ you’re likely to find, but it’s a pretty damn solid representation thereof.

And the turkey smoked to perfection and mouthwatering juicy and full of flavour. Lots of side choices too - particularly enjoyed the cream corn. Guaranteed your eyes are bigger than yours stomach. Highly recommend

Great little outdoor patio area and awesome bar setup. Would love to go back. Only thing I’d love to see change is the amount of single-use containers with the sides and the styrofoam cups. Overall terrific dining experience.

reviews.snippet:
My coworker and I stopped in here for dinner on our first night in Austin. This came as a recommendation from a few locals and they were right on the money. When you walk in the restaurant, you pass a fully-stocked bar and an order line where you can see all the food!

As for the food, this place has unbelievable brisket, 🍖 🐷 🥓 pork, ribs, 🍗 chicken, 🌭 sausage, and more. The smell is amazing. They also have amazing Mac and cheese, corn read, corn, beans, and desserts. They also have a whole wall of free beans, sauces, and cutlery.

This location also has ♿ handicap accessible 🅿️ parking, 🚻 restrooms, and tons of bar and bench seating.

reviews.snippet:
This bbq joint reminds me of the old style joints that are decked out in all wood, where there’s no fancy decor to distract from the good old tasting bbq.
I can’t believe what I’m about to say, but I think the beef rib is the choice to take here.  It is juicy, tender and seasoned right. Ask for a bone will little fat unless you like eating fat. One bone is enough for one to two people depending on how big an eater you are.
I also had the brisket which was salty, but had a nice bark and texture. Dip it in the bbq sauce to dilute the saltiness. As for sides, the cole slaw is a winner since it gives a good contrast to all the meat. For dessert, I chose the banana pudding. It had a tad too much sugar in it that overpowered the taste of banana and felt like you were eating banana flavoured icing.
One big tip is that unless you come often, you don’t know that everything is by the pound and it is weighed after you order it. A 1/4 lbs of meat (about 3 slices) is good enough for one person. One beef rib will feed two people. The person slicing the bbq will try to make you take more meat than what you order. Better to take a little and go back and order more after. We ordered one beef rib and he ended up giving us two. We ordered 1/2 pound of brisket and ended up with a little over a pound.  Keep your eye on the meat slicer and if you think it’s too much tell him to take some back.
Second tip is that there are free pickles, beans and bread next to the bbq sauce.  Keep this in mind when ordering sides.
Third tip is to order dessert after you are done eating to make sure you really need it.
Final tip is that there are takeout containers next to the bbq sauce for you to take leftovers home.
